text: Craig has a phobia of blood and injections. He watches someone having an injection on television,
feels faint and now he is too frightened to turn on his television.
Suggest how applied tension could treat Craig’s phobia so that he can watch television. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by ‘nurture’, including an example from the behavioural explanation of
fear-related disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one weakness of the behavioural explanation of fear-related disorders from the
nurture side of the nature versus nurture debate.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how Dr Begum could use the Beck depression inventory (BDI) with Joan.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one reason why the Beck depression inventory (BDI) is valid.

text: Dr Begum is a clinician who sees a patient, Joan. Joan describes how she spends her day feeling
miserable and not knowing what to do with her time. She thinks it is her own fault because she
cannot decide if she wants to go out, so she stays in. Joan wants to sleep but this is also difficult.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe electro-convulsive therapy (ECT) and cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) for the
treatment and management of schizophrenia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate ECT and CBT for the treatment and management of schizophrenia, including a
discussion about the idiographic versus nomothetic approach.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section B: Consumer Psychology

text: A pizza restaurant is redesigning its menu to encourage more purchases of mushroom pizza.
Suggest two menu design features that could help to sell more mushroom pizzas. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline what is meant by ‘individual and situational explanations’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one reason why ‘overload’ in relation to personal space supports the situational side
of the debate about individual and situational explanations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest one way the manager could use her understanding of ‘point of purchase decisions’
to encourage customers to purchase multiple tins of tomatoes.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
For the suggestion you gave in part (a):
Explain how this could change the customers’ thinking so that they purchase multiple
tins of tomatoes.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
For the suggestion you gave in part (a):
Explain one problem with this suggestion.

text: Customers at a supermarket frequently purchase one tin of tomatoes at a time. The manager of
the supermarket wants to encourage customers to buy multiple tins of tomatoes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the study by North et al. (2003) on musical style and restaurant customers’ spending.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate this study by North et al., including a discussion about ecological validity.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section C: Health Psychology

text: Dr Munsi is concerned that some of her elderly patients with heart disease do not take their
medication every day. Dr Munsi uses the Health Belief Model to design a leaflet to reduce non-
adherence in her elderly patients.
Suggest what Dr Munsi could include in her leaflet to reduce non-adherence in the elderly patients,
using the Health Belief Model. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by ‘application to everyday life’, including a measure of non-adherence
as an example.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one problem with measuring non-adherence in everyday life.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest one way Zainab could encourage her 8-year-old daughter to have a ‘pleasant
life’.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Suggest one way Zainab could encourage her 17-year-old daughter to have a
‘meaningful life’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain one reason why using positive psychology might not lead to an improvement in
mental health for Zainab’s daughters.

text: Zainab has two daughters who are 8 and 17 years old. Zainab wants to help her daughters to
continue to experience good mental health. She reads a book on positive psychology about the
pleasant life, the good life and the meaningful life.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe a study investigating reasons for delay in seeking treatment and a study on
Munchausen syndrome.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate a study investigating reasons for delay in seeking treatment and a study on
Munchausen syndrome, including a discussion about the case study method.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates. 
Section D: Organisational Psychology

text: Arjun is being bullied at work by his manager, Tia. When Arjun is interviewed about the bullying,
he says it started when Tia was promoted to manager. Tia can become stressed at work and
this increases the bullying. Arjun worries about the bullying all the time and thinks that Tia is
encouraging his team to talk to others about him.
Suggest why Tia is bullying Arjun, using your knowledge of the causes of bullying at work. [4]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline Herzberg’s two factor theory of job satisfaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Explain why Herzberg’s two factor theory of job satisfaction can be applied to different
cultures.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Sally manages the production line of a toy factory. A recent survey of her employees has
shown that they are not satisfied with their jobs.
Suggest two job design techniques that Sally could use with her employees to improve their
job satisfaction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
For one of the job design techniques you suggested in part (a):
Explain one weakness of this job design technique.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about:
• token economy used to reduce accidents at work, and
• monitoring accidents and risk events.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about:
• token economy used to reduce accidents at work, and
• monitoring accidents and risk events,
including a discussion about objective and subjective data.
Evaluation in your answer can include strengths, weaknesses and a discussion of issues and
debates.
